ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's first reading links the boast about worldly standing with the following 'until they see what is promised': the unbelievers repeat their taunt until worldly Muslim victory or Judgment reveals their worse standing and weaker forces.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r2.anchor: في هذه الآية وجهان أحدهما أن تكون متصلة بالآية التي هي رابعتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r3.claim: The author calls that linkage extremely remote because a long span and two parenthetical sentences separate the boast from its proposed endpoint; Abū ʿAlī would not allow this.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r3.anchor: انتهى هذا الوجه وهو في غاية البعد لطول الفصل بين قوله قالوا: أي الفريقين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī's second reading connects the phrase with what follows, contrasting their 'better station' and 'finer assembly' with the believers' rivals who are worse in place and weaker in forces; either promised punishment or the Hour is the object they see.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r4.anchor: والثاني أن يتصل بما يليها فذكر نحوا مما قدمناه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r5.claim: The text turns from the deluded person's worldly boasting to the guided person's increase in guidance and enduring good deeds, which replace transient luxury.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p292/r5.anchor: ولما ذكر إمداد الضال في ضلالته وارتباكه في الافتخار بنعم الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r2.claim: The verse was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil, who owed Khabbāb b. al-Aratt for work; he demanded that Khabbāb disbelieve in Muḥammad before he would pay. Khabbāb refused, saying God would raise him after death, and al-ʿĀṣ boasted he would then have wealth and children to pay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r2.anchor: نزلت في العاصي بن وائل عمل له خباب بن الأرت عملا وكان قينا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse concerns al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, who made similar claims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r4.claim: Because seeing can lead to full knowledge and reliable reporting, araʾayta is used idiomatically to mean 'tell'; the fāʾ marks a succeeding story, and the signs are the Qur'an and proofs of resurrection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r4.anchor: ولما كانت رؤية الأشياء سبيلا إلى الإحاطة بها وصحة الخبر عنها استعملوا أرأيت بمعنى أخبر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r5.claim: The majority read waladan with fatḥa in all four occurrences here and in al-Zukhruf; the word denotes the generic category rather than a single child.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ولدا أربعتهن هنا، وفي الزخرف بفتح اللام والواو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r6.speaker: الأعمش وطلحة والكسائي وابن أبي ليلى وابن عيسى الأصبهاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r6.claim: They read wuld with ḍamma on wāw and sukūn on lām; some take it as a broken plural of walad, supported by poetry, and others as synonymous with walad, supported by another poetic line.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وطلحة والكسائي وابن أبي ليلى وابن عيسى الأصبهاني بضم الواو وإسكان اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r7.speaker: عبد الله ويحيى بن يعمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r7.claim: They read wulid with kasra on wāw and still lām.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p293/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ويحيى بن يعمر بكسر الواو وسكون اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r1.claim: Araʾayta follows Sībawayh's pattern: it takes one direct object and a question as its second object; other constructions of araʾayta meaning 'tell me' can be reconciled with this analysis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p294/r1.anchor: وجاء التركيب في أرأيت على الوضع الذي ذكره سيبويه من أنها تتعدى لواحد تنصبه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Arabic opening a-fa-ra’ayta signals a delusion of grandeur or foolishness when introducing the disbeliever’s boast.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: when the address begins with this word, then it means that a person who has delusions of grandeur about himself or something very foolish is being referred to

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Arabic alladhi need not introduce a definite, named person; it can introduce a similitude, as in 16:92, and here depicts a group's mentality.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: At times, it also occurs for a similitude, some very eloquent examples of which are found in the Qur’ān.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The mentality depicted treats blessings as entitlement or personal competence, assumes a birthright to wealth and leadership, and expects to enjoy the same in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: They regard themselves to be entitled to them or think that they are the consequence of their own competence

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Because the boast is foolish and childish, the Qur’an answers it sarcastically and disparagingly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Since this claim is totally foolish and childish too, it is answered in a sarcastic and disparaging way

BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r2.claim: The passage was revealed about al-As ibn Wa'il, who owed Khabbab money, demanded rejection of Muhammad, then mocked resurrection by claiming wealth and children and promising repayment there.
BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r2.anchor: نزلت فيمن سخر بالبعث وهو العاص بن وائل كان لخباب بن الأرت عليه مال

BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r3.claim: The interrogative conveys astonishment at the man's outrageous and brazen claim; the construction means look at the disbeliever in God's signs.
BURSEVI:v5p272#2/r3.anchor: والهمزة للتعجب من حاله والإيذان بأنها من الغرابة والشناعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r1.claim: Khabbab, a creditor and metalworker, says al-ʿĀṣī ibn Wāʾil refused repayment unless he renounced Muhammad; Khabbab refused, and al-ʿĀṣī promised payment after resurrection with wealth and children.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r1.anchor: عن خباب بن الارت قال : كنت رجلا قينا وكان لى العاصى بن وائل دين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r2.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r2.claim: A variant has Khabbab refusing to renounce Muhammad while alive, dead, or resurrected before al-ʿĀṣī repeats his boast.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r2.anchor: لا والله لا اكفر بمحمد ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) حيا ولا ميتا ولا إذا بعثت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r3.speaker: رجل من أصحاب النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r3.claim: Another report says a Companion came with others to collect a debt; the debtor invoked Paradise's riches and swore he would receive wealth, children, and a revealed book after resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r3.anchor: أن رجلا من اصحاب النبى ( صلى الله عليه وسلم ) اتوه يتقاضون دينا لهم عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r4.claim: Some identify the man as al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, but the author says the Khabbab account is established in the canonical collections; Abu Muslim generalizes it to anyone of this character.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r4.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة وقد كانت له اقوال تشبه ذلك وقال أبو مسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r5.claim: The opening question expresses amazement at the unbeliever's bizarre, audacious claim; the fāʾ links it to an implied invitation to look and see.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r5.anchor: الهمزة للتعجيب من حال ذلك الكافر والايذان بانها من الغرابة والشناعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r6.claim: He claims with a profane oath that he will receive wealth and children in the afterlife; reading this as a promise limited to worldly life conflicts with the sound occasion report.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r6.anchor: والمراد انظر اليه فتعجب من حالته البديعه وجراته الشنيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r7.speaker: الطبري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r7.claim: A worldly-only reading of the promised wealth is reported, but it can fit the evidence only if the grant is understood to continue into the afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p129/r7.anchor: واردة في الدنيا كما حكاه الطبرسى عن بعضعم تاباه الاخبار الصحيحة إلا أن يحمل الايتاء على ماقيل على الايتاء المستمر إلى الاخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r1.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r1.claim: The passage most naturally asks the listener to look at and marvel over this unbeliever; a figurative “tell me” reading is less apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r1.anchor: وما قدمنا في معنى الآية هو الأظهر واختارع العلامه أبو السعود

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r2.claim: Another analysis makes “have you seen?” mean “tell me,” using the cause for its result, and takes the question as a figurative command to report; the author critiques this usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r2.anchor: ( ارايت ) في معنى اخبرني بطريق الأستفهام جاريا على اصله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r3.claim: The context may follow the preceding boast about which party has the better gathering, or the earlier denial of resurrection; the former account is more apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r3.anchor: اخبر بقصة هذا الكافر عقيب حديث أولئك الذين قالوا : ( اي الفريقيين خير مقاما ) الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r4.speaker: أبو السعود
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r4.claim: Abu al-Suʿud says “tell me” does not work here as an imperative to someone else, since أَرَأَيْت is conventionally an interrogative request for information.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r4.anchor: المشهور استعمال ( ارايت ) في معنى اخبرني بطريق الأستفهام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي والأعمش وطلحة وابن أبي ليلى وابن عيسى الأصبهاني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r5.claim: They read وُلْدًا with ḍamma and still lām; it may be a plural of ولد or a singular dialect form, and both uses occur in Arabic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r5.anchor: بضم الواو وسكون اللام فقيل : هو جمع ولد كاسد واسد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r6.speaker: عبد الله ويحيى بن يعمر
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r6.claim: They read وِلْدًا with kasra and a still lām, carrying the same sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r6.anchor: بكسر الواو وسكون اللام وهو بمعنى ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r7.claim: Poetic citations support both plural and singular uses of ولد in Arabic.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p130/r7.anchor: فليت فلانا كان في بطن امه وليت فلانا كان ولد حمار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r6.speaker: خباب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r6.claim: Khabbab says al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil owed him wages for metalwork but refused to pay until Khabbab renounced Muhammad; al-ʿAs claimed that after resurrection he would have wealth and children to repay him, prompting this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p253/r6.anchor: خباب قال: كنت قينا فعملت للعاص بن وائل فاجتمع مالي عنده

BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r1.claim: Afaraʾayta uses seeing for comprehensive knowledge and reliable report, introducing a rebuke of the person who rejects the Day after its terrifying consequences were described.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r1.anchor: عن طلب الخير بالرؤية التي هي الطريق إلى الإحاطة بالأشياء علما وخبرة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r2.claim: The denier audaciously claims he will receive great wealth and children in the Hereafter, first disempowering the All-Powerful and then empowering a powerless creature.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p554/r2.anchor: فلم يكفه في جهله تعجيز القادر حتى ضم إليه إقدار العاجز

BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.speaker: خباب
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.claim: Al-Bukhārī reports that Khabbāb, a smith, sought payment for a sword from al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who demanded that he disbelieve in Muhammad; al-ʿĀṣ then claimed he would be resurrected wealthy with children and repay him, and the verse was revealed.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p555/r2.anchor: قال : كنت قينا بمكة فعملت للعاص بن وائل السهمي سيفا

QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r11.claim: By implication, a believer who hopes well of God may expect fulfillment because the believer is under covenant with God, who does not break His covenant.
QUSHAYRI:v2p247/r11.anchor: أن المؤمن إذا ظن بالله تعالى ظنا جميلا ، أو أمل منه أشياء كثيرة فالله تعالى يحققها له ، ويصدق ظنه لأنه على عهد مع الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r1.claim: The passage branches from the resurrection denier’s claim and exposes the same delusion; it points to the exchange between Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt and al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, reported in the Ṣaḥīḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r1.anchor: والآية تشير إلى قصة خباب بن الأرت مع العاصي بن وائل السهمي . ففي ( الصحيح )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r2.claim: Khabbāb, a Muslim sword-maker, sought payment for a sword sold on credit; al-ʿĀṣ refused unless he renounced Muhammad, and Khabbāb refused.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r2.anchor: فجاء خباب يتقاضى دينه من العاصي فقال له العاصي بن وائل : لا أقضيكه حتى تكفر بمحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r3.claim: When Khabbāb said God would cause al-ʿĀṣ to die and then raise him, al-ʿĀṣ mockingly promised to have wealth and children then and repay the debt; al-ʿĀṣ is the verse’s target.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r3.anchor: قال ( العاصي متهكما ) : إذا كان ذلك فسيكون لي مال وولد وعند ذلك أقضيك دينك ) . فنزلت هذه الآية في ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r4.claim: A-fa-raʾayta conveys astonishment; “seeing” is figurative for knowing an extraordinary story as if it were visually witnessed, and the relative clause explains the source of wonder.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r4.anchor: والاستفهام في { أفرأيت } مستعمل في التعجيب من كفر هذا الكافر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r5.claim: The address applies to any suitable hearer, though it may specifically address the Prophet; al-āyāt here are the Quran, including its resurrection passages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r5.anchor: والخطاب لكل من يصلح للخطاب فلم يرد به معين . ويجوز أن يكون خطابا للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r6.claim: Walad is a collective noun for children; most readers use the standard form, while Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use wuld with a still wāw in the four occurrences in this sūra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p158/r6.anchor: والولد : اسم جمع لولد المفرد ، وكذلك قرأه الجمهور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r11.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r11.claim: Most commentators identify the unbeliever as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī; the author recounts his dispute with Khabbāb as the occasion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r11.anchor: والذي كفر يعني به العاصي بن وائل السمهي، قاله جمهور المفسرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r12.claim: Khabbāb, a blacksmith and creditor, demanded payment; al-ʿĀṣ refused unless he renounced Muhammad, which Khabbāb refused.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r12.anchor: وكان خبره أن خباب بن الأرت كان قينا في الجاهلية فعمل له عملا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r13.speaker: العاصي بن وائل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r13.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ mocked resurrection, then claimed he would have wealth and children after death and repay Khabbāb; the verse came down about this exchange.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r13.anchor: قال العاصي: أو مبعوث أنا بعد الموت؟ قال خباب نعم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r14.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verse was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who made similar claims.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r14.anchor: وقال الحسن نزلت الآية في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r15.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r15.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read waladan with fatḥa as a generic singular, except for the passage in Sūrat Nūḥ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r15.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو «وولدا» على معنى اسم الجنس بفتح الواو واللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r16.speaker: نافع وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r16.claim: Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir use fatḥa throughout the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r16.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وابن عامر بفتح الواو في كل القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r17.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r17.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read wuldan with ḍamma and quiescent lām throughout the Quran.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r17.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «وولدا» بضم الواو وسكون اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r18.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r18.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads wuldan with kasra on the wāw and quiescent lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r18.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود «ولدا» بكسر الواو وسكون اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r19.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r19.claim: Some interpret wuld with ḍamma as a plural of walad and cite poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30/r19.anchor: واختلف مع ضم الواو فقال بعضهم: هو جمع «ولد كأسد وأسد»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r1.claim: Others say wuld means walad, citing a poem about being born the child of a donkey.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم هو بمعنى الولد واحتجوا بقول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī says the Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī readings are singular when singular is intended and plural when plural is intended.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي في قراءة حمزة والكسائي ما كان منه مفردا قصد به المفرد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r3.speaker: الأخفش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash distinguishes walad as son or daughter and wuld as family or parent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r3.anchor: وقال الأخفش: الولد الابن والابنة، والولد الأهل والوالد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r4.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r4.claim: Another scholar says walad means the womb from which someone came; Abū ʿAlī transmits this in al-Ḥujja.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p30#2/r4.anchor: وقال غيره: والولد بطن الذي هو منه، حكاه أبو علي في الحجة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r1.claim: The Ṣaḥīḥayn report from Khabbab says his debtor al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil refused repayment unless Khabbab renounced Muhammad; when Khabbab refused, al-ʿAs promised wealth and children after resurrection. Most interpreters identify him as the occasion for the verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r1.anchor: من حديث مسروق عن خباب بن الأرت قال كنت رجلا قينا أي حدادا وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r2.claim: A second account says the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, though the majority accept the Khabbab report.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r2.anchor: والثاني أنها نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة وهذا مروي عن الحسن والمفسرون على الأول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r3.claim: These readers use an open wāw in waladan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر بفتح الواو

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r4.claim: These readers use a ḍamma on the wāw; al-Farraʾ says both forms are dialects, not a plural distinction, though Qays treats walad as collective and walad as singular.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بضم الواو وقال الفراء وهما لغتان كالعدم والعدم وليس يجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r5.claim: He may have meant that he would receive wealth and children in Paradise according to the believers' claim, or in this world.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p260/r5.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما أنه أراد في الجنة على زعمكم والثاني في الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.claim: Khabbab says al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il refused to pay his debt unless he disavowed Muhammad; when Khabbab refused, al-ʿAs claimed he would have wealth and children after resurrection, prompting revelation. The canonical collections transmit it through several routes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r1.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كنت رجلا قينا، وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين، فأتيته أتقاضاه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.claim: Al-ʿAwfi transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's account that companions sought debts from al-ʿAs, who argued that since they expected heavenly wealth and scripture, he too would receive wealth, children, and a book like theirs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r3.anchor: وقال العوفي عن ابن عباس: إن رجالا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا يطلبون العاص بن وائل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r4.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r4.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and others identify the man in these verses as al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p259/r4.anchor: وهكذا قال مجاهد، وقتادة، وغيرهم: إنها نزلت في العاص بن وائل.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r1.claim: Readers differ between fathah and dammah on walad, but both readings share a meaning; poetry witnesses the forms, and one view makes dammah plural and fathah singular in the Qays dialect.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p260/r1.anchor: قرأ بعضهم بفتح "الواو" من "ولدا" وقرأ آخرون بضمها، وهو بمعناه

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r1.claim: These readers use the ḍamma form of وولدا in four places in this surah and two elsewhere.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: (وولدا) بضم الواو وسكون اللام

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r2.claim: These readers use the ḍamma form in Noah and the fatḥa form throughout the other Qur'an.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب في سورة (نوح) بضم الواو

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r3.claim: These readers use fatḥa on both letters throughout the Qur'an.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر بفتح الواو واللام في جميع القرآن

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r4.claim: One view treats walad and wuld as equivalent, supported by two poetic lines.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r4.anchor: أنهما بمعنى واحد كالعدم والعدم، والحزن والحزن

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r5.claim: A Qays dialect uses walad as a collective and wuld for one child.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r5.anchor: أن قيسا تجعل الولد جمعا، والولد واحدا

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r6.claim: Walad derives from birth and offspring; lexical discussion contrasts a foreign-born, Arab-raised slave woman with one born in Muslim lands.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r6.anchor: الولد: ولد الرجل، وأصله من الولادة

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r7.speaker: القتبي
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r7.claim: Al-Qutaybī defines a talīda as born abroad and raised in Arab lands, unlike a woman born in Islamic lands.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r7.anchor: قال [القتبي]: التليدة التي ولدت ببلاد العجم

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r8.speaker: ابن شميل
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r8.claim: Ibn Shumayl says talīd and mawlūd both mean people born in one's own household.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r8.anchor: قال ابن شميل: التليد والمولد واحد

JISHUMI:v6p4604/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r9.claim: Another proposed etymology links walad to secure upbringing; mawlid can also mean newly coined speech.
JISHUMI:v6p4604/r9.anchor: والمولد كل كلام محدث لمن يكن في القديم فاستحدث

JISHUMI:v6p4606/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، خباب
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r4.claim: They report that the verse was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil al-Sahmī.
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r4.anchor: في العاص بن وائل السهمي، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وخباب

JISHUMI:v6p4606/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r5.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r5.claim: They transmit the story of Khabbāb demanding his deferred wages, which al-ʿĀṣ mocked by promising payment in Paradise.
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r5.anchor: حتى أقضيك في الجنة استهزاء، فنزلت الآية: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا، عن مقاتل والكلبي

JISHUMI:v6p4606/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r6.claim: Al-Aṣamm rejects the story of al-ʿĀṣ mocking Khabbāb’s claim for wages.
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r6.anchor: عن مقاتل والكلبي، وأنكر القصة الأصم

JISHUMI:v6p4606/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r7.speaker: خباب
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r7.claim: Khabbāb says al-ʿĀṣ demanded that he renounce Muhammad before paying a small debt; al-ʿĀṣ then promised payment after resurrection.
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r7.anchor: وعن خباب: حتى كان لي عليه دانق فأتيته أطلبه، فقال: حتى تكفر بمحمد

JISHUMI:v6p4606/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r8.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the verse was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
JISHUMI:v6p4606/r8.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v6p4610/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r5.claim: God reproaches and threatens the man for making the boastful claim about what he will receive.
JISHUMI:v6p4610/r5.anchor: وتدل على أن ذلك القول فعله لذلك وبخه به وأوعده عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r1.claim: أفرأيت means “report/tell”; the fāʾ links this disbeliever's story after the previous people's story.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r1.anchor: في معنى ( أخبر ) والفاء جاءت لإفادة معناها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ولدا as a plural of ولد or as a synonym for it; Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar has another kasra-vowelled reading.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r6.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the passage was revealed about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, though the widely held view identifies al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r6.anchor: عن الحسن رحمه الله : نزلت في الوليد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r7.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r7.claim: Khabāb reports that al-ʿĀṣ owed him money and demanded that Khabāb disbelieve in Muḥammad before he would repay it; Khabāb refused even after death or resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r7.anchor: قال خباب بن الأرت : ( 674 ) كان لي عليه دين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r8.claim: In Khabāb's account, al-ʿĀṣ asks whether he will be resurrected and boasts he will then have wealth and children with which to pay.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r8.anchor: فإني إذا مت بعثت ؟ قلت : نعم . قال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r9.claim: A second report says Khabāb made jewelry for him and demanded payment; al-ʿĀṣ deferred it, claiming he would have gold, silver, and silk in Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r9.anchor: صاغ له خباب حليا فاقتضاه الأجر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r10.claim: كلا is a rebuke and warning: he is mistaken in imagining and wishing this, and must stop.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p40/r10.anchor: ردع وتنبيه على الخطأ أي : هو مخطيء

FARRA:v2p170/r12.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p170/r12.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p170/r12.claim: A reading of afaraʾayta alladhī omits the hamza.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r1.speaker: جبار
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r1.claim: The verse may concern al-As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi; Ibn Abbas and Mujahid agree.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r1.anchor: في العاص بن وائل السهمي , قاله جبار وابن عباس ومجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r2.claim: Another view says it concerns al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r2.anchor: الثاني : في الوليد بن المغيرة , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r3.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read wuld with damma, others walad with fatḥa; one view makes them synonyms (supported by al-Harith ibn Hilliza's line), while another says the damma is plural in Qays and the fatḥa singular.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي { وولدا } بضم الواو , وقرأ الباقون بفتحها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r4.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r4.claim: The boast of future wealth and children may mock the promised afterlife reward for worship and obedience.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r4.anchor: أنه أراد في الجنة استهزاء بما وعد الله على طاعته وعبادته , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r5.claim: The majority say he means wealth and children in this world: either if he keeps his ancestors' religion and idols, or because he assumes prosperity proves his religion is true.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p387/r5.anchor: أنه أراد في الدنيا , وهو قول الجمهور . وفيه وجهان محتملان

MUQATIL:19:77-78/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r1.claim: Muqatil says the passage was revealed about al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil after Khabbāb made jewelry for him and asked for his fee.
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r1.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل بن هشام بن سعد بن سعيد بن عمرو بن هصيص

MUQATIL:19:77-78/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r2.claim: The phrase about God's signs means the verses of the Qur’an.
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r2.anchor: { أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا } ، آيات القرآن

MUQATIL:19:77-78/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r3.speaker: العاص
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r3.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ mocked Khabbāb by saying he would receive better wealth and children in Paradise and repay him there.
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r3.anchor: قال العاص: فميعاد ما بيننا الجنة، { وقال لأوتين } في الجنة

MUQATIL:19:77-78/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r4.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ spoke mockingly because he did not believe the Qur’an’s promises of reward and punishment.
MUQATIL:19:77-78/r4.anchor: يقول ذلك مستهزئا؛ لأنه لا يؤمن بما في القرآن من الثواب والعقاب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.speaker: حمزة وعلي
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.claim: Hamza and Ali read ولد with a ḍamma on wāw and a still lām in four places here and in al-Zukhruf and Nuh; it can be a collective like أسد or mean child like العرب means Arabs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r1.anchor: وبضم الواو وسكون اللام في اربعة مواضع ههنا وفي الزخرف ونوح حمزة وعلي جمع ولد كأسد في أسد أو بمعنى الولد كالعرب في العرب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.claim: أفرأيت means tell or report, since seeing leads to knowledge and truth of report; the fā signals continuing with this disbeliever's story after the previous one.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r2.anchor: ولما كانت رؤية الأشياء طريقا إلى العلم بها وصحة الخبر عنها استعملوا أرأيت في معنى أخبر والفاء أفادت التعقيب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p46#2/r3.claim: لأوتين is the response to an implied oath.

MAJAZ:v2p9/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p9/r8.speaker: بعضهم
MAJAZ:v2p9/r8.claim: Some preserve the hamza when رأيت is interrogative, treating it as unchanged; Abū al-Aswad’s أريت omits the hamza, while al-Mutawakkil al-Laythī’s أرأيت retains it.
MAJAZ:v2p9/r8.anchor: «أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا» (77) إذا استفهموا ب «رأيت» فمنهم من يدعها على حالها كأنه لم يعده أحدث فيها شيئا

MAJAZ:v2p9/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p9/r9.speaker: بعضهم
MAJAZ:v2p9/r9.claim: Others think interrogative رأيت has been altered and drop its hamza; Abū al-Aswad’s verse exemplifies the omitted-hamza form.
MAJAZ:v2p9/r9.anchor: ومنهم من يرى أنه أحدث فيها شيئا فيدع همزتها، قال أبو الأسود: أريت امرأ كنت لم أبله

MAJAZ:v2p9/r10.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p9/r10.speaker: المتوكل الليثي
MAJAZ:v2p9/r10.claim: Al-Mutawakkil al-Laythī’s verse retains the hamza in أرأيت.
MAJAZ:v2p9/r10.anchor: وقال المتوكل الليثى: أرأيت إن أهلكت مالى كله

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.speaker: خباب
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.claim: Khabbāb had a debt owed by al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil; when pressed to deny Muḥammad, he refused until the debtor died and was raised, and al-ʿĀṣ mocked that he would repay when restored to wealth and children. The report is transmitted by Muslim and Bukhārī.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r1.anchor: عن خباب قال كان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فأتيته أتقاضاه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say blacksmith Khabbāb had made jewelry for al-ʿĀṣ; al-ʿĀṣ mocked repayment in Paradise, claiming he would have wealth there and Khabbāb no greater entitlement.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان خباب قينا فصاغ للعاص حليا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r3.claim: The boast about being granted wealth and children concerns al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, named in the reports.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r8.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read “waladan” with ḍamma, while others use fatḥa; they may be dialect synonyms, though Qays uses the ḍamma form as plural and the fatḥa as singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-80/r8.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «وولدا» بضم الواو، والباقون بفتحها

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r1.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r1.claim: A line by al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza uses the fatḥa form “waladan” to illustrate the word.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r1.anchor: ولقد رأيت معاشرا قد ثمروا مالا وولدا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r2.speaker: قيس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r2.claim: Qays treats the ḍamma form as plural and the fatḥa form as singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r2.anchor: أن قيسا تجعل الولد بالضم جمعا والولد بالفتح واحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r3.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r3.claim: Al-Māwardī lists a Paradise boast mocking God’s promise, or a claim to worldly wealth either from remaining in ancestral religion or as proof of religious truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r3.anchor: وفي قوله تعالى: { لأوتين مالا وولدا } وجهان

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says al-Kalbī’s Paradise reading best fits the hadiths, especially their explicit wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r4.anchor: قول الكلبي أشبه بظاهر الأحاديث، بل نصها يدل على ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r5.speaker: مسروق
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r5.claim: Masrūq heard Khabbāb report that al-ʿĀṣ expected wealth and children in the afterlife and promised repayment; al-Tirmidhī graded the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:77-79/r5.anchor: قال الترمذي: هذا حديث حسن صحيح

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r1.claim: After establishing resurrection and answering deniers, God now recounts their mockery of resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر الدلائل أولا على صحة البعث

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read وُلدا, explained either as a plural of ولد like أُسُد or as a synonym for offspring like عَرَب.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي ولدا وهو جمع ولد كأسد في أسد

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r3.speaker: يحيى بن يعمر
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Yaʿmar is reported to read ولد with kasra on the wāw.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r3.anchor: وعن يحيى بن يعمر ولدا بالكسر

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r4.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the verse was revealed about al-Walid ibn al-Mughira.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r4.anchor: وعن الحسن نزلت الآية في الوليد بن المغيرة

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r5.claim: The famous occasion identifies the man as al-As ibn Wa'il; Khabbab ibn al-Aratt said that when he sought repayment, al-As demanded that he disbelieve in Muhammad first.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r5.anchor: والمشهورة أنها في العاص بن وائل ، قال خباب بن الأرت : كان لي عليه دين

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r6.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r6.claim: In Khabbab's report, al-As asked whether Khabbab believed he would be resurrected; Khabbab affirmed it, and al-As claimed he would then have wealth and children to repay him.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r6.anchor: قلت : نعم . قال : إني بعثت وجئتني فسيكون لي ثم مال وولد فأعطيك

RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r7.claim: An alternate report says Khabbab made jewelry for al-As; when he asked for payment, al-As postponed it, invoking their claim of resurrection and Paradise's gold, silver, and silk.
RAZI-FULL:v21p213/r7.anchor: وقيل : صاغ خباب له حليا فاقتضاه فطلب الأجرة

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r1.claim: Wealth and children repeatedly symbolize worldly goods but also worldly trials.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r1.anchor: Wealth and children are mentioned repeatedly in the Quran as emblematic of the good things of this world

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r2.speaker: Ṭ, Ṭs, W
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r2.claim: The verse reportedly answers al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, who mocked a creditor by claiming that, if resurrected, he would possess wealth and children and repay the debt then.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r2.anchor: would be able to repay his debt then (Ṭ, Ṭs, W)

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r3.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r3.claim: An alternate identification names al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah as the disbeliever who made the claim.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r3.anchor: Some say that the disbeliever who spoke these words was al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah (Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:19:77/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r4.claim: The statement may also express an attitude common to disbelievers generally.
STUDYQURAN:19:77/r4.anchor: might also be intended to convey an attitude common among other disbelievers and thus to apply generally.

TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.speaker: خباب
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.claim: Khabbāb says al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil owed him money and refused to pay unless he renounced Muhammad; al-ʿĀṣ boasted that after resurrection he would have wealth and children, prompting these verses.
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r1.anchor: عن خباب، قال: كنت رجلا قينا، وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين، فأتيته أتقاضاه، فقال: والله لا أقضيك

TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when companions collected a debt, al-ʿĀṣ mocked their promise of Paradise and boasted he would have wealth, children, and a book like theirs in the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r2.anchor: فقال: ألستم تزعمون أن في الجنة فضة وذهبا وحريرا، ومن كل الثمرات؟ قالوا: بلى، قال: فإن موعدكم الآخرة،

TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the person who says he will receive wealth and children as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله: {لأوتين مالا وولدا} [مريم: 77] قال: العاص بن وائل يقوله

TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r4.claim: Qatāda recounts an unbeliever who mocked the promise of Paradise's wealth and clothing while refusing to believe the revealed Book.
TAB-FULL:v15p617#2/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا} [مريم: 77] فذكر لنا أن رجالا

TAB-FULL:v15p620/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r1.speaker: خباب
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r1.claim: Khabbāb recounts that al-ʿĀṣ refused his payment until he disbelieved in Muhammad, then claimed he would have money and children after resurrection; Khabbāb reported this to the Prophet and the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r1.anchor: عن مسروق، قال: قال خباب بن الأرت: كنت قينا بمكة، فكنت أعمل للعاص بن وائل، فاجتمعت لي عليه دراهم، فجئت لأتقاضاه،

TAB-FULL:v15p620/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r2.claim: Medinan, Basran, and some Kufan readers open the wāw in walad throughout; Abū ʿAmr uses the damma only in Noah, while most Kufans use it in several passages.
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r2.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء المدينة والبصرة وبعض أهل الكوفة: {وولدا} [الكهف: 39] بفتح الواو من الولد

TAB-FULL:v15p620/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r3.claim: Some grammarians say walad with an open or rounded wāw has the same meaning, citing poetry and the proverb that children are born from one's heels.
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: ضمها وفتحها واحد، وإنما هما لغتان، مثل قولهم العدم والعدم، والحزن والحزن.

TAB-FULL:v15p620/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r4.speaker: قيس
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r4.claim: A report says Qays uses walad as a plural and walid as the singular, perhaps explaining why some readers distinguish the forms.
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر لي أن قيسا تجعل الولد جمعا، والولد واحدا.

TAB-FULL:v15p620/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r5.claim: Al-Tabari says both open and rounded wāw readings are correct dialect forms, but prefers the more common open form.
TAB-FULL:v15p620/r5.anchor: أن الفتح في الواو من الولد والضم فيها بمعنى واحد، وهما لغتان، فبأيتهما قرأ القارئ فمصيب الصواب،

TABATABAI:19:75-77/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:75-77/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:75-77/r10.claim: The next four verses portray someone who heard the disbelievers, was swayed to join them, and claimed that adopting their polytheism would bring wealth and children.
TABATABAI:19:75-77/r10.anchor: أن بعض الناس ممن آمن بالنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أو كان في معرض ذلك بعدما سمع قول الكفار مال إليهم ولحق بهم قائلا لأوتين مالا وولدا

TABATABAI:19:78-79/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r1.speaker: الأكثر
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r1.claim: Most commentators, following reports about the occasion of revelation, identify the speaker as a Quraysh polytheist who said this to Khabbāb when asked to repay a debt, claiming he would receive wealth and children in Paradise.
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r1.anchor: ما ذكره الأكثر بالبناء على ما ورد من سبب النزول أن الجملة قول أحد المتعرقين في الشرك من قريش خاطب به خباب بن الأرت

TABATABAI:19:78-79/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects that setting: Quraysh polytheists did not affirm resurrection, so a promise of post-resurrection wealth would be mockery, which the following argument cannot answer.

TABATABAI:19:78-79/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم المفسر
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r3.claim: Abū Muslim says the verse applies generally to anyone with this trait; the author also judges this reading inadequate to the passage’s context.
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r3.anchor: ما نقل عن أبي مسلم المفسر أن الآية عامة فيمن له هذه الصفة

TABATABAI:19:78-79/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r4.claim: The opening is an exclamation linked by فاء to the prior boast: this person’s disbelief and promise share the same belief that paganism brings worldly success.
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r4.anchor: مسوق للتعجيب، وكلمة { أفرأيت } كلمة تعجيب وقد فرعه بفاء التفريع

TABATABAI:19:78-79/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r5.claim: The oath lām and emphatic nūn show that the speaker swears he will receive wealth and children, treating disbelief as a blessed path to power and happiness.
TABATABAI:19:78-79/r5.anchor: وقد أقسم بذلك كما يشهد به لام القسم ونون التأكيد

TABATABAI:19:80/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.speaker: الأكثر
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.claim: On the majority reading, the speaker is ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil or al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra, who swears he will receive wealth and children in Paradise after resurrection; God asks whether he knows the unseen or has a covenant, then strips him of possessions and brings him alone.
TABATABAI:19:80/r4.anchor: بناء على كونه ناظرا إلى الإيتاء في الآخرة كما اختاره الأكثر فمعنى الآيات كما فسروها تعجب من الذي كفر بآياتنا وهو عاص بن وائل أو وليد بن المغيرة

TABATABAI:19:80/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:19:80/r5.claim: A report in Tafsīr al-Qummī identifies the man as ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil; when Khabbāb sought his debt, he promised to pay it with better wealth in Paradise.
TABATABAI:19:80/r5.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:19:80/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80/r6.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
TABATABAI:19:80/r6.claim: Khabbāb reports that ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil refused to repay his debt unless Khabbāb disbelieved in Muḥammad; Khabbāb refused even if ʿĀṣ died and was raised.
TABATABAI:19:80/r6.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال كنت رجلا قينا وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين فأتيته أتقاضاه

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.claim: The report continues that ʿĀṣ said he would return after death with wealth and children to repay Khabbāb; the author notes similar accounts from al-Ṭabarānī, Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr via al-Ḥasan and an unnamed Companion, and Ibn ʿAbbās via Companions, without grading them.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r1.anchor: قال فإني إذا مت ثم بعثت جئتني ولي ثم مال وولد فاعطيك

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.claim: The reports do not fit the context: they make the saying a mockery by someone who denied resurrection, whereas the passage answers it with a serious argument.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r2.anchor: على صراحتها في كونها كلمة استهزاء لا تنطبق على الآية

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r3.claim: Even if the statement were a taunt meant to corner Khabbāb rather than a sincere claim, mentioning children lacks a rationale because early Muslims were not known to teach procreation in Paradise.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r3.anchor: لم يكن لذكر الولد مع المال وجه وكفاه أن يقول لأوتين مالا

TABATABAI:19:80#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r4.claim: The emphatic oath, unqualified promise of being given wealth, and question about unseen knowledge or covenant are inexplicable as mere dialectical cornering.
TABATABAI:19:80#2/r4.anchor: ولم يكن للقسم والتأكيد البالغ في قوله { لأوتين } وجه

TABRISI:19:76-82/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:76-82/r5.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
TABRISI:19:76-82/r5.claim: A report identified as sound says al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil owed Khabbāb money and refused payment unless Khabbāb renounced Muḥammad; Khabbāb refused until death and resurrection.
TABRISI:19:76-82/r5.anchor: روي في الصحيح عن خباب بن الأرت قال كنت رجلا غنيا وكان لي على العاص بن وائل دين

TABRISI:19:76-82/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:76-82/r6.speaker: العاص بن وائل
TABRISI:19:76-82/r6.claim: Al-ʿĀṣ claimed he would be resurrected with wealth and children and repay Khabbāb then; the verse was revealed in response.
TABRISI:19:76-82/r6.anchor: فسوف أقضيك دينك إذا رجعت إلى مال وولد قال فنزلت الآية

TABRISI:19:76-82/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:76-82/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:76-82/r11.claim: Afaraʾayta expresses amazement at the denier of God’s proofs, whether Qurʾānic or other proofs; Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid identify him as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
TABRISI:19:76-82/r11.anchor: أفرأيت كلمة تعجيب ومعناه أرأيت هذا الكافر الذي كفر بأدلتنا من القرآن وغيره

TABRISI:19:78-82/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:19:78-82/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the denier as al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r1.anchor: وقيل: الوليد بن المغيرة عن الحسن

TABRISI:19:78-82/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:19:78-82/r2.claim: Abū Muslim reads the example generally: it applies to anyone with this trait.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو عام فيمن له هذه الصفة عن أبي مسلم

TABRISI:19:78-82/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r3.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:19:78-82/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says the promise of wealth and children is sarcastic: the man boasts that he will receive them in Paradise.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r3.anchor: استهزاء أي لأعطين مالا وولدا في الجنة عن الكلبي

TABRISI:19:78-82/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:78-82/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:78-82/r4.claim: Alternatively, he means he will receive wealth and children in this life if he stays with his fathers’ religion and worship of idols.
TABRISI:19:78-82/r4.anchor: وقيل: أعطي في الدنيا أي إن أقمت على دين أبائي وعبادة آلهتي

THALABI:v6p228/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p228/r12.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
THALABI:v6p228/r12.claim: Khabbab reports that al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil, who owed him money, demanded that he renounce Muhammad before paying; al-ʿAs claimed he would have wealth and children after death, prompting the revelation.
THALABI:v6p228/r12.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كان لي دين على العاص فأتيته أتقاضاه فقال: لا والله حتى تكفر بمحمد

THALABI:v6p229/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r1.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
THALABI:v6p229/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say Khabbab was a metalworker owed delayed wages by al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil; when Khabbab refused to leave Islam, al-ʿAs mocked that he would repay him in Paradise with a greater share.
THALABI:v6p229/r1.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان خباب بن الأرت قينا وكان يعمل للعاص بن وائل السهمي

THALABI:v6p229/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p229/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p229/r2.claim: The boast la-utin means “I will surely be given” wealth and children.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وجماعة أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r1.claim: The verse concerns al-ʿAs ibn Waʾil, who owed Khabbab money and demanded that he reject Muhammad’s God before being repaid; he mocked resurrection and promised payment after it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وجماعة أهل التفسير: (نزلت في العاص بن وائل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r2.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r2.claim: Al-ʿAs told Khabbab that if his claim were true, he would have a greater share than Khabbab; this occasioned the revelation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: (قال لخباب: لئن كان ما تقول حقا فإني لأفضل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r3.claim: La-utay means I will certainly be given; an oath is implicit, and he claims wealth and children in Paradise after Resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r3.anchor: {وقال لأوتين} لأعطين أي: والله لأوتين القسم # مضمر {مالا وولدا} يعني في الجنة بعد البعث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r4.claim: Both walad and wuld are read; al-Layth says walad can be singular or collective, masculine or feminine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r4.anchor: وقرئ: ولدا، وولدا (¬1). قال الليث: (الولد اسم يجمع الواحد والكثير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r5.speaker: الزجاج والفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r5.claim: The two forms walad and wuld are equivalent, as are the paired forms ʿarab/ʿarab, ʿajam/ʿajam, and bukhl/bukhl; poetry illustrates the usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج: (الولد والولد واحد مثل العرب، والعرب، والعجم، والعجم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r6.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r6.claim: The proverb about one’s child coming from one’s heels’ blood and a poem about a donkey’s offspring show that the rounded form can be singular; Qays uses walad collectively and wuld singly.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r6.anchor: واحتج على استعمال المضموم في الواحد بقول العرب في المثل: (ولدك من دمى عقبيك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r7.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r7.claim: Walad can be used for one child or several.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r7.anchor: وقال ابن السكيت: (الولد يكون واحدا وجمعا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r8.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r8.claim: Walad is like fulk, whose form can be singular or plural, and can be a plural of walad like asad/asud and thamar/thumur.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p310/r8.anchor: قال أبو علي: (هو كالفلك الذي يكون مرة جمعا ومرة واحدا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r2.claim: The disbeliever boasting of future wealth and children is al-As ibn Wa'il; when Khabbab demanded payment, al-As mocked him with claims about his share of Paradise's gold and silver.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r2.anchor: أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا } يعني: العاص بن وائل { وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا } وذلك أن خبابا اقتضى دينا له عليه، فقال: ألستم تزعمون أن في الجنة ذهبا وفضة؟

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r3.claim: Al-As said he would have a better share if their claim about Paradise were true and told Khabbab to wait for repayment there; his promised wealth and children mean in Paradise.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:76-78/r3.anchor: ولئن كان ما تقولون حقا فإني لأفضل نصيبا منك، فأخرني حتى أقضيك في الجنة، استهزاء، فذلك قوله: { لأوتين مالا وولدا } يعني: في الجنة،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r3.claim: The disbeliever's claim to receive wealth and children refers to the afterlife.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r3.anchor: قوله: {أفرأيت الذي كفر بآياتنا وقال لأوتين مالا وولدا} [مريم: 77] أي في الآخرة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.claim: Khabbāb reports that al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil withheld his wages unless he disavowed Muhammad, then promised to repay after resurrection from future wealth and children; Khabbāb told the Prophet, and these verses were revealed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r6.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كنت قينا في الجاهلية فعملت للعاصي بن وائل حتى اجتمعت لي عنده دراهم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.claim: Qatāda reports that a Companion seeking a debt from a polytheist heard the debtor promise repayment in Paradise, claiming he would have wealth and children there; the challenge asks if he had seen the Unseen.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p241/r7.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: ذكر لنا أن رجلا من أصحاب النبي عليه السلام أتى رجلا من المشركين

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r1.claim: The reported occasion concerns the poor Muslim blacksmith Khabbāb, who demanded his debt from al-ʿĀṣ b. Wāʾil; al-ʿĀṣ refused repayment unless Khabbāb rejected Muhammad.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r1.anchor: Fakir bir müslüman olup Mekke’de demircilikle meşgul olan Habbâb b. Eret’in, yaptığı bir işten dolayı müşriklerin ileri gelenlerinden Âs b. Vâil’de alacağı vardı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r2.speaker: Habbâb b. Eret
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r2.claim: Khabbāb swore he would never reject Muhammad even until al-ʿĀṣ died and was raised; al-ʿĀṣ claimed he would have wealth and children then and repay him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:77/r2.anchor: “Allah’a yemin ederim ki sen ölüp tekrar dirilinceye kadar onu asla inkâr etmem” dedi. Âs, “Gerçekten ben ölüp tekrar dirilecek miyim?” diye sordu

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146/r1.claim: Khabbāb reports that al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil withheld his debt unless Khabbāb disbelieved in Muhammad; when Khabbāb refused until after his death and resurrection, al-ʿĀṣ boasted he would have wealth and children there, and the verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p146/r1.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال جئت العاصي بن وائل السهمي أتقاضاه حقا لي عنده فقال لا أعطينك حتى تكفر بمحمد

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r2.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r2.claim: Khabbāb ibn al-Aratt says al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil refused to repay a debt unless Khabbāb disbelieved in Muhammad, then promised payment after resurrection when he would have wealth and children; al-Bukhārī and Muslim transmit the report.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r2.anchor: عن خباب بن الأرت قال: كان لي دين على العاص بن وائل فأتيته أتقاضاه فقال: لا والله حتى تكفر بمحمد

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r3.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī and Muqātil say Khabbāb, a metalworker employed by al-ʿĀṣ, demanded his wages; al-ʿĀṣ mocked resurrection and proposed paying him in Paradise, claiming he would receive more than Khabbāb.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p301/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: كان خباب بن الأرت قينا، وكان يعمل للعاص بن وائل السهمي، وكان العاص يؤخر حقه

SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r1.claim: The ف in أفرأيت signals that this disbeliever's story follows the preceding one; أرأيت means tell me, with the relative first object and the question second.
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r1.anchor: قوله: { أفرأيت }: عطف بالفاء إيذانا بإفادة التعقيب كأنه قيل:

SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r2.claim: لأوتين answers an implicit oath, and the oath clause is the complement of القول.
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r2.anchor: و " لأوتين " جواب قسم مضمر، والجملة القسمية كلها في محل نصب بالقول.

SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r3.claim: The word occurs here, in Maryam 88 and 91, al-Zukhruf 81, and Nuh 21; the two Hamza-family readers use ḍamma/sukūn, while Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr join them only at Nuh.
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r3.anchor: وقوله هنا: " وولدا " وفيها قالوا اتخذ الرحمن ولدا

SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r4.speaker: الأخوان
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r4.claim: The two readers use ḍamma and sukūn; Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, and ʿAsim use fatḥa throughout the listed passages.
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r4.anchor: قرأ الأربعة الأخوان بضم الواو وسكون اللام.

SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r5.claim: The double-fatḥa reading is a singular noun used with collective force.
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r5.anchor: فأما القراءة بفتحتين فواضحة وهو اسم مفرد قائم مقام الجمع.

SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r6.claim: The ḍamma/sukūn form is either synonymous with ولد, like عرب/عرب, or its plural; a cited poem witnesses the plural use.
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r6.anchor: وقيل: بل هي جمع لولد نحو: أسد وأسد، وأنشدوا على ذلك:

SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r7.speaker: عبد الله ويحيى بن يعمر
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r7.claim: They read it with kasra, a dialect; it may be a passive participle meaning a child born, like القبض for المقبوض.
SAMIN-DURR:19:77/r7.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله ويحيى بن يعمر " وولدا " بكسر الواو، وهي لغة في الولد،

ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r4.claim: The variant الولد with ḍamma can be a plural like أسد, can be singular or plural, or can mean the same as ولد, as with العرب and العجم.
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r4.anchor: فمن قرأ ولدا بالضم فهو على وجهين

ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r5.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r5.claim: The denier is identified in the exegesis as al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil.
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r5.anchor: وقد جاء في التفسير أنه يعنى به العاص بن وائل

ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r6.speaker: خباب
ZAJJAJ:v3p344/r6.claim: Khabbāb recounts that as a pre-Islamic blacksmith he was owed money by al-ʿĀṣ, who refused payment unless he rejected Muhammad; Khabbāb refused, and al-ʿĀṣ mockingly promised to repay after resurrection with wealth and children.

ASAD-NOTES:19:76#n66/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:76#n66/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:19:76#n66/r1.claim: The passage criticizes material values that exclude moral concerns and equate worldly success with wealth and children.
ASAD-NOTES:19:76#n66/r1.anchor: namely, the insistence on material values to the exclusion of all moral considerations

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr open وَلَد except in Noah, where they round it; Nafi, Asim, and Ibn Amir open all six, while Hamza and al-Kisai round all.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r1.anchor: فقرأهن ابن كثير وأبو عمرو: وولدا بالفتح إلا في سورة نوح: (ماله وولده) فإنهما قرءاه بضم الواو

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r2.claim: Abu al-Hasan says ولد can mean a son or daughter, while وُلد can include a person's family and children; another view associates it with one's own body.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r2.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: الولد: الابن والابنة، قال: والولد: هم الأهل والولد.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.claim: Al-Farisi connects ولد with wealth and children, citing Quranic pairings of المال and البنون or الأولاد.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: الولد: هو ما ذكر في التنزيل في غير موضع مع المال، قال: المال والبنون زينة الحياة الدنيا [الكهف/ 46]

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r4.speaker: الفراء
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r4.claim: Al-Farra quotes an Asad proverb about a child as one's own bloodline and reports Muadh al-Harra's view that ولد is collective.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r4.anchor: وروى محمد بن السري، عن أحمد بن يحيى عن الفراء قال: من أمثال بني أسد: ولدك من دمي عقبك .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r5.claim: ولد may be a plural like أسد or a singular whose form matches its plural, like بخل and عرب; this qualifies Muadh's claim that it is only collective.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p210/r5.anchor: الذي قال معاذ وجه، ويجوز أن يكون جمعا كأسد وأسد، ونمر ونمر،

IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r4.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r4.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr open wāw in wuladan except at Nūḥ 71:21, where they use ḍamma wāw and quiescent lām. Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir always open wāw; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī quiesce lām with ḍamma wāw throughout.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p411/r4.anchor: 20 واختلفوا فى ضم الواو وفتحها من قوله ﴿ وولدا ﴾ 77 فى ستة مواضع فى مريم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p412/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p412/r1.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p412/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī use ḍamma wāw and quiescent lām in all the cited Quran forms.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p412/r1.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائى بضم الواو وسكون اللام فى كل القرآن

QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#1/r1.claim: Facilitating hamza drops it from raʾā for lighter pronunciation while retaining the same grammatical meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#1/r1.anchor: Hamza facilitation — hamza of raʾā dropped entirely; phonologically lighter; grammatically identical meaning

QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#2/r1.claim: The marked transitional hamza represents an intermediate sound between full realization and full elision, reflecting early dialectal variation.
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#2/r1.anchor: Hamza rest/transitional — hamza marked as a middle phonological state between full realization and full drop

QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#3/r1.claim: Prolonging hamza to a long ā creates an emphatic pause before the relative clause and stretches the interrogative moment.
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#3/r1.anchor: Hamza prolonged into long ā vowel; creates emphatic pause before the relative clause

QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#4/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#4/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#4/r1.claim: The split pause-and-continuation double reading presents hamza as a live phonological question in early transmission.
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:2#4/r1.anchor: Split waqf/waṣl double-reading variant; unusual form suggesting hamza was a live phonological question

QIRAAT-ER:19:77:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:13#1/r1.claim: Wuld is a collective offspring noun, intensifying the boast from one heir to a dynasty rather than one child.
QIRAAT-ER:19:77:13#1/r1.anchor: Vowel change: wuld (collective plural) — offspring as a group/mass noun; intensifies the boast

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.claim: Khabbab recounts that al-As ibn Wa'il withheld wages until he renounced Muhammad and boasted of future wealth; after Khabbab told the Prophet, the passage was revealed.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p13#4/r1.anchor: عن أبي الضحى عن مسروق قال قال خباب بن الأرت كنت قينا وكنت أعمل للعاص بن وائل فاجتمع لي عليه دراهم

BURHAN:v2p349/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p349/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p349/r1.claim: The interrogative hamza can precede the conditional particle إن; هل cannot occupy that position.
BURHAN:v2p349/r1.anchor: ولا تقول هل إن تخرج اخرج معك

BURHAN:v2p349/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p349/r3.speaker: ابن الطراوة
BURHAN:v2p349/r3.claim: Ibn al-Tarawa claims the hamza is always balanced by an expressed or understood alternative; the author reports al-Saffar’s objection that every interrogative asks for certainty and hamza examples with alternatives are abundant.
BURHAN:v2p349/r3.anchor: زعم ابن الطراوة انها لاتكون ابدا الا معادلة

BURHAN:v2p349/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p349/r4.speaker: الصفار
BURHAN:v2p349/r4.claim: Al-Saffar rejects Ibn al-Tarawa’s restriction: هل قام زيد also asks whether he stood or not, and hamza questions without an expressed alternative are common.
BURHAN:v2p349/r4.anchor: ورد عليه الصفار وقال لا فرق بينها وبين غيرها فإنك اذا قلت هل قام زيد

BURHAN:v2p349/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p349/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p349/r5.claim: The hamza precedes conjunctions and other interrogative particles because it is the original question particle and has initial position; conjunctions otherwise cannot precede part of an interrogative clause.
BURHAN:v2p349/r5.anchor: وانما خولف هذا في الهمزة لانها اصل ادوات الاستفهام

BURHAN:v4p178/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p178/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p178/r1.claim: هل is more explicitly restricted to verbs than the hamza; nominal clauses after هل emphasize that the requested qualities are present and established, unlike verbal forms that suggest renewal.
BURHAN:v4p178/r1.anchor: وهل أظهر في الاختصاص بالفعل من الهمزة

BURHAN:v4p178/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p178/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p178/r2.claim: The hamza can move beyond its basic interrogative use to convey denial, affirmation, report, and other meanings discussed under interrogation.
BURHAN:v4p178/r2.anchor: واعلم أنه يعدل بالهمزة عن أصلها فيتجوز بها عن النفي والإيجاب والتقرير وغير ذلك المعاني السالفة في بحث الاستفهام

BURHAN:v4p178/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p178/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p178/r3.claim: When hamza precedes رأيت, the verb no longer means seeing with eye or mind; it means ‘tell me,’ semantically takes a preposition, but grammatically takes a direct object.
BURHAN:v4p178/r3.anchor: وإذا دخلت على رأيت امتنع إن تكون من رؤية البصر أو القلب وصارت بمعنى أخبرني

BURHAN:v4p178/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p178/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p178/r4.claim: Hamza before لم conveys either reminder or astonishment at something momentous; in either case the construction warns the hearer.
BURHAN:v4p178/r4.anchor: وإذا دخلت على لم أفادت معنيين

BURHAN:v4p178/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p178/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p178/r5.claim: أم is a connective substituting for repetition of a noun or verb; grammarians variously analyze it as connective, interrogative connective, or أو with a changed consonant. It divides into connected and disconnected forms; the connected form asks for identification, follows a hamza, and has one clause on both sides.
BURHAN:v4p178/r5.anchor: أم حرف عطف نائب عن تكرير الاسم والفعل

ITQAN:v4p389/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p389/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p389/r7.claim: The person who disbelieved is al-As ibn Wa'il.
ITQAN:v4p389/r7.anchor: ﴿ أفرأيت الذي كفر ﴾ هو العاصي بن وائل

NASHR:v2p318/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p318/r9.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
NASHR:v2p318/r9.claim: Across four occurrences in Maryam and one in al-Zukhruf, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read ولد with ḍamma on wāw and sukūn on lām; the others use fatḥa on both.
NASHR:v2p318/r9.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي بضم الواو، وإسكان اللام في الخمسة،

BUKHARI:2091/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:2091/r1.speaker: خباب
BUKHARI:2091/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il withheld his debt until he disbelieved, then claimed he would regain wealth and children after resurrection; the revelation rebuts that claim.
BUKHARI:2091/r1.anchor: عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ قَيْنًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، وَكَانَ لِي عَلَى الْعَاصِ بْنِ وَائِلٍ دَيْنٌ

BUKHARI:4733/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4733/r1.speaker: خباب
BUKHARI:4733/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il refused payment unless he disbelieved, then asserted he would have wealth and children after resurrection; the verses expose this claim as baseless.
BUKHARI:4733/r1.anchor: عَنْ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ أَبِي الضُّحَى، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ قَيْنًا بِمَكَّةَ،

BUKHARI:4735/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4735/r1.speaker: خباب
BUKHARI:4735/r1.claim: Khabbab reports that al-As ibn Wa'il promised to pay his debt from wealth and children after resurrection; the passage was revealed to reject that boast and foretell punishment and his solitary return to God.
BUKHARI:4735/r1.anchor: عَنْ أَبِي الضُّحَى، عَنْ مَسْرُوقٍ، عَنْ خَبَّابٍ، قَالَ كُنْتُ رَجُلًا قَيِّنًا، وَكَانَ لِي عَلَى الْعَاصِي بْنِ وَائِلٍ دَيْنٌ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r1.claim: Umar urged people to consult their poetic canon, saying Arab poetry contains interpretations of scripture and meanings of speech.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r1.anchor: فقال عمر عليكم بديوانكم لا تضلوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls poetry the Arabs’ register and says obscure Quranic vocabulary should be clarified from their poetry, which he often recited when asked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r2.anchor: وعن ابن عباس الشعر ديوان العرب فإذا خفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r5.speaker: عكرمة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r5.claim: Ikrima explained zanīm as an illegitimate child and cited a poem as evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r5.anchor: وسئل عكرمة ما معنى الزنيم ، فقال هو ولد الزنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r6.speaker: أحمد بن حنبل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r6.claim: Ahmad ibn Hanbal reportedly said he disliked a person’s use of a poetic line to explain Quranic meaning; Ibn Ashur calls the reported response puzzling.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r6.anchor: فمما يؤثر عن أحمد بن حنبل رحمه الله ، أنه سئل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r7.claim: If Ahmad’s disapproval is authentic, Ibn Ashur thinks he likely objected to using poetry to challenge the soundness of Quranic wording, as some unbelievers did.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r7.anchor: لعله يريد كراهة أن يذكر الشعر لإثبات صحة ألفاظ القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r8.claim: Ibn al-Rawandi challenged Ibn al-Aʿrabi over whether “garment of piety” was Arabic; Ibn al-Aʿrabi answered with a pun denying that he lacked mastery of Arabic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r8.anchor: قال لابن الأعرابي : أتقول العرب لباس التقوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r11.claim: Prophetic explanations of Quran are few; Ibn Atiyya’s report from Aisha that the Prophet explained only a limited number concerns unseen matters and generalities requiring revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r11.anchor: قال ابن عطية عن عائشة ما كان رسول الله يفسر من القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r15.claim: The referent in 19:77 is al-As ibn Waʾil in his dispute with Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, as reported in al-Bukhari’s tafsir of al-Muddaththir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p22/r15.anchor: العاصي بن وائل السهمي في خصومته بينه وبين خباب بن الأرت
